name: Translators
intro: Where translation is accurate and the voice is clear, and where it is an empty wrapper.

apps.title: Google Translate
apps.verdict: The category benchmark for coverage: 100+ languages, text, camera, voice, conversation mode, and offline packs. Free. Recent version issues include camera freezing and the conversation mode cutting people off mid-sentence.
apps.loved: The camera translates text on images instantly without tapping a button. Offline language packs work without internet, which is critical when traveling. Language coverage is the widest in the category.
apps.weak: Conversation mode is too aggressive about starting: recognition fires automatically and layers the translation over the other person while they are still speaking. The camera sometimes freezes and switches to photo mode instead of staying in real-time.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who needs a free translator with the broadest language coverage and offline capability. Especially travelers reading signs and menus through the camera.

quotes.text: The auto-detection in Conversation Mode is too aggressive. When sharing one phone with a friend, the app constantly cuts me off and blasts out translations while I'm still talking. It causes a confusing overlap of audio that ruins the conversation. Please bring back the manual recording controls

GT has been my go-to for auto translating as I read text in Japanese for some time. But recently, the camera is freezing constantly and forcing you to take a picture. The auto-translate as I go is essential, and this update has made reading in real time next to impossible.

apps.title: Yandex Translate
apps.verdict: A strong text translator with an AI mode for complex sentences. Built-in dictionary with word saving and flashcard review. Photo translation is unreliable and noticeably lags behind the text mode. Known issue: the app mutes background music with no way to turn that off. Entering Chinese via pinyin breaks the keyboard layout. AI mode sometimes auto-switches back to fast mode.
apps.loved: Word study built right into the translator: save, review, and remember words without switching to another app.
apps.weak: Photo translation has no auto-detect and produces unpredictable results. Chinese character input via pinyin is technically broken.
apps.whoFor: Russian-speaking users learning a language who want to translate and save words to a personal vocabulary list in one place.

apps.title: DeepL Translate
apps.verdict: The best text translator in this batch for accuracy, which users with professional language knowledge confirm. Camera works but is slow (about 5 seconds per frame). Voice synthesis sounds dated. The app stopped remembering the language pair between sessions after one update.
apps.loved: Translation accuracy when handling nuance: alternative phrasings, gender agreement, and register are all taken into account.
apps.weak: After every launch the app resets the language pair to the default and does not remember your preference.
apps.whoFor: People who translate carefully and care about precise wording rather than speed.

quotes.text: Use it for French. Very accurate and I love the option for alternative words and sentences. But the sound of the voice playback is horrible and sounds like a robot. This seems unacceptable in the age of AI. The sound of the voices in Google Translate sound like real humans and are far superior.

Much better at translating than Google and nearly all other competitors, however, the speed of camera translation is way too slow so I almost always choose Google instead. In most real world use cases time is critical, and waiting/freezing for almost 5 seconds isn't really acceptable.

The app is 100% accurate but why is it so hard to get dialects? I am trying to translate words into American English yet it translates into the British version and it is really hard to try to choose the dialect, I have to struggle in order to get the one I am trying to translate.

apps.title: Microsoft Translator
apps.verdict: A key tool in the category. Free, compact (around 20 MB), and no subscription required. Supports group conversations via QR code. Recent updates have hurt voice mode stability.
apps.loved: Group conversation mode: multiple participants join via QR code and each see the translation in their own language in real time. Free with no usage limits.
apps.weak: After recent updates, voice recognition started mixing up languages and dropping words. There is a 1,000-character cap on text input, and the app does not tell you until you hit it.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who needs a reliable free translator without subscriptions, especially for group meetings or business travel where translation into multiple languages is needed at once.

quotes.text: Initially I liked this app very much. For context I am hard of hearing and this app helps with quick conversations at help desks like libraries for example. I use 'converse' so it listens continuously rather than every time clicking on listen (in translate). But then slowly it started giving issues.
The text exceeded the maximum length of 1000 characters. Please use shorter text
Tried to upload a PDF from Files. Could not find a means by which to upload any documents from anywhere in the known universe. It was the primary reason I downloaded it. I will be deleting it now.

apps.title: UDictionary Translator
apps.verdict: Works as an overlay translator directly over WhatsApp and Instagram without switching apps. Built-in grammar check with multiple suggestions. Word list and personal dictionary mode. Weak spots: long messages get cut off, no full-screen support on iPad.
apps.loved: Overlay mode: translate text in any app without copying or leaving. Multiple translation engines in a single interface.
apps.weak: Long texts do not display in full. Grammar check does not show a correction when there is only one error.
apps.whoFor: Users who message in social apps in a foreign language and want to translate right inside the chat without switching apps.

quotes.text: This application performs adequately for translating text in platforms like WhatsApp and Instagram, however, it frequently struggles to render lengthy messages in their entirety. As a workaround, I often resort to Google Translate for more comprehensive translations.

apps.title: Dialog - Translate Speech
apps.verdict: A specialized app for live two-way speech translation. Niche, but with a loyal audience. Main issue: voice stops working at the slightest background noise or pause.
apps.loved: Two-way conversation mode enables a real dialogue: each person speaks into the phone, the app auto-detects the language, and reads the translation aloud. Users praise accuracy on supported languages.
apps.weak: Voice recognition cuts out on any pause longer than half a second and requires louder, slower speech than natural conversation. In the free version, ads interrupt translation in the middle of someone speaking.
apps.whoFor: People who need a tool for a live face-to-face conversation with someone in a foreign language and are willing to hold the phone between them and take turns speaking.

apps.title: Spanish Translator Offline
apps.verdict: A dedicated Spanish-English translator with an offline mode. Handles standard Spanish well, but regional dialects (especially rural Mexican Spanish) produce errors. Offline is only available in the paid version, which the name implies otherwise.
apps.loved: The offline dictionary works without internet, which is critical when traveling. Shows example sentences in context, not just a bare translation.
apps.weak: Voice input does not recognize informal speech or regional variants. Offline is in the app name but only available behind a paywall.
apps.whoFor: A traveler to Spanish-speaking countries who needs an offline dictionary with context examples rather than a live conversation mode.

quotes.text: This app is title 'offline' but you only get offline if you upgrade.

The particular part of Mexico, I am in they do not comprehend most of this translator. Spanish in Mexico is very regional. I am having a hard time using this translator in my current location it is a shame I paid for a lifetime and I cannot use it.

apps.title: Translator - Translate Box
apps.verdict: The main feature is showing multiple translation engines side by side (including DeepL), so you can compare results and pick the best one. Users working in Korean note it gets the right translation in cases where Google misses it. Tagalog is weak. Ads are aggressive in the free version and sometimes keep showing up even with a subscription.
apps.loved: Side-by-side output from multiple translation engines on one screen. Unique among competitors in this price range.
apps.weak: Tagalog and some less common languages translate poorly. Ads keep interrupting even after paying for a subscription.
apps.whoFor: Users working with Korean, Chinese, or other languages where cross-checking multiple engines matters.

apps.title: iTranslate Translator
apps.verdict: A full-featured translator with text, voice, and a keyboard extension. Covers over 100 languages. Relevant for the category.
apps.loved: The built-in keyboard lets you translate right inside WhatsApp and other messengers without switching apps. Listening to pronunciation helps you both understand and reproduce a word.
apps.weak: Translation quality is inconsistent across languages: Italian works better than French, and Greek transliteration contains errors. Voice translation occasionally produces wrong phrases without any warning.
apps.whoFor: Travelers and people who regularly message with foreign contacts and want to translate without leaving the chat.

quotes.text: I really like the application. It works well. I mainly use the keyboard because it translates messages really well on apps like Whatsapp. I just really wish it had the swipe feature.

apps.title: iTranslate Voice
apps.verdict: An app originally sold as a one-time purchase now requires a subscription to access the same features. Voice translation works but cuts off recording after one or two words when there is any background noise. Only one voice option (female), no choice. The most frustrating scenario: losing previously purchased access after an update.
apps.loved: Voice translation launches with a single button tap and no extra steps when the environment is quiet.
apps.weak: Recording cuts off within a second at any background sound and cannot capture full sentences.
apps.whoFor: Users in a quiet environment who need a simple voice translator without a camera.

quotes.text: Speaks too fast but very helpful to use. The Computer voice is a bit harsh sometimes as well.

Trying live voice translate and most of the time I hit the button and it listens for about half a second then stops and says 'Sorry I am not sure what you said'. Can not get it to translate more than one or two words at a time.
This app translates English to Spanish well but Spanish to English is abysmal.

apps.title: AI Phone:Call&Voice Translator
apps.verdict: A specialized product for translating live phone calls and video calls in real time. A unique mechanic for the category. Monetization is dual-layer: a subscription plus per-minute credits, which confuses users.
apps.loved: Translation during a live phone call works: both sides hear the translation in real time without switching apps. Supports video calls through WhatsApp.
apps.weak: The dual monetization creates confusion: after subscribing, users discover that call minutes still draw from a separate credit pool. It is not a bug but an intentional model, yet it reads as a bait-and-switch.
apps.whoFor: People who regularly call family or business partners in another language and want to hear the translation right in the call without a third screen.

apps.title: Translator »
apps.verdict: Voice translation works for live communication: users report using it on the job to understand Spanish-speaking coworkers. Camera is unreliable and sometimes produces nonsensical output. Japanese is inaccurate according to native speakers. Language flags are sometimes wrong (Tagalog shows the East Timor flag).
apps.loved: Voice mode with real recognition that is accurate enough for a working conversation in Spanish.
apps.weak: Camera translation is unstable. Accuracy for Japanese and several Asian languages is low according to native speakers.
apps.whoFor: People relocating to or working in a Spanish-speaking environment who need a quick voice bridge.

quotes.text: This app has Portuguese from Brazil, but the Portuguese from Portugal is from Brazil. We don't use the same these words in Portugal. These words are spoken in Brazil only.

apps.title: Live Translator - AI Translate
apps.verdict: A live translator with a continuous conversation mode where users confirm it genuinely does not require a button press after every phrase. That is rare among competitors. But there is a hidden paywall: $59 for real-time mode on top of the base subscription.
apps.loved: Conversation mode with no manual trigger: both people speak in turn, the app detects pauses and switches languages on its own. Users share a pair of earbuds.
apps.weak: Live mode costs an extra $59 on top of the main subscription, and this is not disclosed before purchase. Keyboard translation is slow (up to 30 seconds). No offline support.
apps.whoFor: A traveler who needs a hands-free conversation mode with no button-pressing and is willing to pay twice for it.

quotes.text: ONLY app i have found that does not require constant button pushing to talk. True conversation mode, i use one earbud and partner uses the other. If they add offline mode where downloaded languages can be used outside of wifi i would give 5 stars

I just purchased this app because I am traveling to South Korea and I want to be able to understand the signs in the airport as well as communicate with the taxi drivers, however the speech playback speed is way to fast and a bit glitched. If there is a way to slow it down that would be helpful!
The keyboard translate from messages or WhatsApp is very slow. Sometimes it takes up to 30 seconds to translate. Other Translate programs are much much faster.

apps.title: Speak & Translate - Translator
apps.verdict: A text and speech translator for live communication that has been around for over ten years. Basic accuracy is decent, but stability is a concern.
apps.loved: One-phone conversation mode works well for real exchanges: users report that complex two-way conversations felt natural. Supports less common languages like Swahili.
apps.weak: The app frequently opens to a white screen and can take up to two minutes to load. Voice recognition is inconsistent: sometimes it picks up nothing, and sometimes it plays back translation at an unnaturally high speed.
apps.whoFor: People who regularly communicate with speakers of one specific foreign language and value voice mode, and are willing to tolerate an unstable launch.

quotes.text: Persian and many more languages are not available in voice mode not benifited

apps.title: Translation Voice Translator
apps.verdict: A basic translator with voice input. Real users apply it for communicating with Spanish-speaking coworkers on the job. Conversation mode occasionally produces errors that confuse the other person. The app is unstable and sometimes rebuilds itself from scratch, requiring a reinstall. Language settings do not persist.
apps.loved: Voice input works for basic on-the-spot communication.
apps.weak: Conversation mode has lag and errors in Spanish that confuse the other person. Language pair settings do not save between sessions.
apps.whoFor: Occasional travel and brief work conversations with Spanish-speaking coworkers.

apps.title: Translator Keyboard - Language
apps.verdict: A translator keyboard that plugs into any app and translates as you type. A genuinely useful idea. But the $10-per-week price kills any goodwill: it is more expensive than most premium translators on the market.
apps.loved: The built-in keyboard works in any messenger without switching apps. Translation right in the input field is a mechanic without a real equivalent among most competitors.
apps.weak: The keyboard runs noticeably slower than the default. Translation quality drops for languages beyond Spanish. Security concern: the keyboard requires 'full access,' which means it can potentially read anything you type.
apps.whoFor: Someone who regularly writes in two languages in messengers and is willing to pay for speed. At $10 a week that is a very narrow audience.

apps.title: Translator with Speech
apps.verdict: Works as a conversation translator for English-to-Spanish in simple situations: users have genuinely communicated through it with housekeepers and Spanish-speaking coworkers. Camera translation is inaccurate, switching the source language away from English breaks voice input, and ads are aggressive and non-dismissible.
apps.loved: Voice dialogue mode works for EN-ES without extra steps.
apps.weak: When the base language is changed away from English, voice input stops recognizing speech.
apps.whoFor: Tourists who need a quick EN-ES conversation mode without high accuracy requirements.

quotes.text: When translating to Filipino language I can not get sound. I need the sound to learn how to pronounce a word. Why isn't there with tagalog?

apps.title: Scan & Translate+ Text Grabber
apps.verdict: Once a strong OCR translator with a unique feature: translated text was overlaid directly onto the image, preserving visual context. After updates that feature was removed, and the app became a generic scan-and-translate tool with worse stability.
apps.loved: OCR handles handwritten and mixed text well (users cite a church document in Russian as an example). Works with uncommon languages.
apps.weak: The signature feature of overlaying translation onto the photo was removed in a recent version. The server goes offline periodically, support does not respond, and the contact email is outdated.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who needs to read text from old documents or handwritten materials, and is willing to deal with instability.

quotes.text: This app looked at an old Russian church document that had both printed and scripted Russian language. Most of what it saw it translated however there were names on the document and those of course were left in Russian

apps.title: Translate AI Pocket Translator
apps.verdict: A wrapper around Google Translate with three input modes (text, voice, camera) in one app. The engine is identical to the free Google Translate, but this version adds ads and a subscription. Voice input frequently fails on the first try and requires repeating the phrase. Useful only if you specifically want all three modes in a single interface.
apps.loved: Text, voice, and camera switch without changing screens.
apps.weak: Voice input does not fire on the first attempt and often requires two or three repetitions before it recognizes the phrase.
apps.whoFor: Users who are comfortable with Google Translate but want camera and voice on a single screen.

apps.title: Voice Translator: AI Translate
apps.verdict: A voice translator focused on conversation mode. Serious gaps in voice language coverage: Norwegian, Arabic, and others are text-only even though the marketing promises otherwise.
apps.loved: A keyboard button overlay over any app lets you translate directly inside a messenger without copying text. Some users note good accuracy for Korean.
apps.weak: Voice translation is unreliable: the app frequently fails to detect the language or produces an incorrect translation. The actual list of languages with voice support is much shorter than advertised.
apps.whoFor: A user who wants a quick translate-button overlay on top of any app and who works within a pair of popular languages.

apps.title: Translator Guru: Voice & Text
apps.verdict: A keyboard translator with voice input. The main value is the keyboard extension for messengers. Stability suffers: the translate button occasionally gets replaced by a paywall button, and the backspace key glitches.
apps.loved: The keyboard extension lets you translate right in the input field of any messenger without opening a separate app. Works in WhatsApp and iMessage.
apps.weak: The keyboard interface is unstable: backspace sometimes deletes the whole text instead of one character, and the translate button disappears and gets replaced by a paywall. Voice recognition cannot handle accents.
apps.whoFor: Users who frequently message in a foreign language in messengers and want to translate without copying text.

quotes.text: App doesn't appear to understand an American Midwest accent

I do like this keyboard. It translated very well. Only thing it glitches when trying to use the backspace button. It doesn't respond fluidly and when you press it too many times it deletes the whole message.

apps.title: Instant Voice Translate
apps.verdict: Voice recording cuts off mid-sentence. The microphone has poor capture even on new devices (iPhone 16). Persian is missing (over 200 million speakers). The Turkish-to-Spanish pair does not work. After subscribing, voice translation does not function at all for some users.
apps.loved: In ideal conditions (clear speech, supported language pair) transcription is accurate and fast enough.
apps.weak: The voice engine cuts off sentences and struggles to capture audio, and that is the core feature of the app.
apps.whoFor: Hard to recommend: the primary feature is unreliable.

apps.title: Translator ·
apps.verdict: A general-purpose translator with a wide language selection in text mode. Camera and conversation are subscription-only. Ads between every translation in the free version make it practically unusable.
apps.loved: Wide language coverage with above-average text translation accuracy. Users mention it as a better option than Google Translate for Japanese.
apps.weak: Voice and photo modes are fully behind a paywall with no warning before download. Language settings reset after every translation in the free version.
apps.whoFor: A subscriber who needs wide language coverage and solid text translation without ads.

quotes.text: This app has Portuguese from Brazil, but the Portuguese from Portugal is from Brazil. We don't use the same these words in Portugal. These words are spoken in Brazil only.

apps.title: Translate Free - Language Translator & Dictionary
apps.verdict: An outdated translator built on Google Translate with a nice selection of Spanish regional dialects. Has not been updated in years and occasionally stops working after an iOS update. Paid voice is unstable. Useful only as a free text translator for short phrases.
apps.loved: Regional Spanish dialect selection (Mexican, Latin American) with no extra configuration required.
apps.weak: Long text translations get cut off at an undisclosed word limit in the free version.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who needs a free EN-ES text translator without extra features.

quotes.text: I have tried the free version and like it very much. I tried translating a text message to a friend but it only translated about half. Is there a limitation on the amount of words that can be translated both in the free and Pro version?

apps.title: Translate Now - AI Translator
apps.verdict: A translator with text, voice, camera, and AI features. Technically well-equipped, but monetization is aggressive: $10 a week for most features. The store reputation does not match the real user experience.
apps.loved: ChatGPT integration delivers more contextual translations of phrases and idioms where classic engines give a literal result. The keyboard extension works for free.
apps.weak: Most features (camera, live translation, voice) are locked without a subscription, and this is not explained before install. Connection errors on live translation reproduce even on a solid internet connection.
apps.whoFor: A user who needs fast text translation and is willing to pay for full AI feature access with full price transparency up front.

apps.title: Translate Photo & Camera Scan
apps.verdict: A camera translator with a strict limit on free scans (10 per day, resets every 24 hours). OCR fails on handwriting, small fonts, and small objects. The server occasionally returns an error instead of a translation. The concept is right, the execution is unstable.
apps.loved: Recognizes text from photos in real-world conditions: signs, menus, printed documents.
apps.weak: The scan limit runs out in a single session, after which you must wait 24 hours or pay.
apps.whoFor: Tourists who need to translate a sign or menu once in a while, not anyone working with documents regularly.

apps.title: Talk & Translate AI Translator
apps.verdict: The advertised core feature, real-time speech translation, does not work: the microphone fails to pick up speech or returns an error. Text translation is also unstable. Users report malware after reinstalling, which makes this app potentially unsafe.
apps.loved: Conversation mode works for short phrases on a good connection.
apps.weak: Real-time voice input does not recognize speech and produces no translation.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone.

quotes.text: I want to know how the Kanji is pronounced in Japanese, but for some reason, the voice button won't work. This app is still useful, though, but I still need some help.

apps.title: Translate Me - Live Translator
apps.verdict: A translator that claims a live mode but in practice works phrase-by-phrase like any other. The interface is cluttered with ads, voice stream cuts off too quickly, and certain language pairs are unavailable in conversation mode.
apps.loved: Supports many languages for basic text translation and launches quickly.
apps.weak: Voice mode does not show the translation long enough before the next line comes in and the result disappears. Conversation mode is unavailable for several language pairs including Ukrainian.
apps.whoFor: A tourist who needs to look up a word once in a while and only if they can tolerate an ad after every single request.

quotes.text: Was looking to translate spoken English to/from Ukrainian since Ukrainian is listed as a supported language. When we got to the conversation mode, clicking on the microphone popped up the message that translations were not available for this language pair.

apps.title: Persian Translator Offline
apps.verdict: An app with one real feature, text translation between English and Persian, and an advertised but non-functional voice mode. 'Offline' in the name does not match reality. An ad plays before the audio button, which is silent anyway. Useful only as an offline dictionary for those who read Persian.
apps.loved: Single-word translation with examples and the dictionary database work without a network connection.
apps.weak: TTS for Persian phrases produces no audio in either the paid or free version.
apps.whoFor: Persian readers who need an offline dictionary and do not need voice output.

quotes.text: Your out if luck if you haven't perfected your Farsi writing skills, because you can not listen to the audio. Despite this, they still make you watch an ad when clicking on the speak button only for it to not work.

apps.title: Voice Language Translator Pro
apps.verdict: Bulgarian voice output runs through a Russian voice pack, and native speakers hear a foreign accent with wrong intonation. Persian is not supported for voice input. Urdu is missing despite Hindi being present. Does not exceed Google Translate in any capability but costs money.
apps.loved: Text translation on popular language pairs works adequately.
apps.weak: Text-to-speech uses non-native voice packs for several languages, making voice mode useless for native speakers of those languages.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone.

apps.title: Photo Translator - Translate
apps.verdict: A photo translator with working OCR for simple text, but the free version is deliberately capped at three translations per day. Accuracy drops on complex fonts and long paragraphs. Ads are aggressive.
apps.loved: Recognizes text from photos quickly and handles short printed text in popular languages.
apps.weak: The 3-photo-per-day limit cuts off functionality before the user can even evaluate quality. Camera focus is unstable, and Japanese and Chinese characters in long paragraphs translate poorly.
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants to read one label or sign a day and does not mind ads. Not suitable for regular use.

quotes.text: The app is fine, but it depends on the language and length of what you are trying to translate. For example: I was trying to transite these two russian words from my sheet music. The app worked. However, when i needed it to translate a paragraph of Chinese, the translation was awful.

apps.title: Translate Voice App Translator
apps.verdict: A voice translator with incomplete language coverage: Chinese as a source language is unavailable entirely, and switching language pairs causes the app to crash. The interface is confusing with no clear way to start a text translation. Charges are applied without confirmation.
apps.loved: Voice input works for Arabic and common European languages.
apps.weak: Switching language pair causes the app to crash, so you cannot test different combinations before buying.
apps.whoFor: Arabic-speaking users who need one-way voice translation.

apps.title: Translate
apps.verdict: Basic translations of simple words get it wrong (piña is rendered as 'Rose' instead of 'pineapple'). Japanese breaks at the sentence level. Language coverage is narrow with no Hungarian, Tamil, or Cantonese. Little practical value for real communication.
apps.loved: The conversation mode occasionally produces unexpected output from unrecognized input, which users describe as amusing.
apps.weak: The translation engine makes systematic errors even on common language pairs. The language set does not cover common user requests.

quotes.text: Takes forever to find a translation. Even if I download the languages I need it still tries to find using the internet which can be extremely slow when traveling internationally. Now I have to put my iphone into airplane mode to get an instant offline translation which is annoying.

apps.title: Camera Translator - AI OCR +
apps.verdict: A camera OCR translator where the free mode functions only as a demo for selling a subscription. Users report that paid functionality does not always activate, the camera angle is awkward, and ads appear after every scan.
apps.loved: Fast recognition in good lighting. Works with non-standard languages like Venezuelan Spanish.
apps.weak: The camera does not focus at a normal distance and requires holding the object too far away. Payment does not always activate the subscription, and support does not respond.
apps.whoFor: Practically no one. Competitors (including the native iOS camera translator) do the same thing without these issues.

quotes.text: Wish this was a live translation. But you have to take a picture and then see the translation. I am using it to translate screens so it is difficult to see what options I should choose since the text does not line up with the location on the screen.

apps.title: Voice Translator: Translate AI
apps.verdict: Voice translation produces poor results: speech rate is unnatural and stress patterns are wrong. A Hindi translation produced a dangerously distorted result (a phrase about routes came out as aggressive text). No translation history. Almost no practical value.
apps.loved: The app launches and delivers text translation. That is the full list of positives based on reviews.
apps.weak: The voice engine speaks the translation at a speed and accent that native speakers cannot understand. Hindi recognition quality introduces semantic errors that are dangerous in real conversation.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended in its current state.

quotes.text: My wife speaks cebuano so I thought this would be well with the $100+ bucks, then I see it only translates cebuano to English via text. Voice translate is not available for that particular combination.

apps.title: Translator GO: AI Translate
apps.verdict: Claims live and offline translation, but offline does not work after payment, camera output is unreadable, and the voice engine sounds like the 1980s. A concrete failure: one user paid for a year and got a frozen screen.
apps.loved: In theory supports a large language set. One French user reports a successful conversation mode experience, which appears to be an isolated case.
apps.weak: Offline mode does not activate after payment. The voice engine is outdated, conversation mode only works EN to Hindi with no reverse direction. The camera shows a white block over the translation.
apps.whoFor: No one. Google Translate does everything this app claims, for free and far more reliably.

quotes.text: I got this to speak to people in India. Spoken English to Hindi is great! But spoken Hindi to English doesn't work at all. So it is not useful for me and certainly not worth paying for.

I got this app for my trip to Rome and Greece. I got it mainly for the Greek part due to Apple did have Greek as an option. Liked the idea that I could use it off line. When the time came I couldn't use it. I paid for the offline version and it never worked so I ended up having to turn my travel data on.

apps.title: AI Photo Translator
apps.verdict: Marketed as a photo translator, but the camera is locked behind a paywall from the very first tap. Korean is shown on the app icon but is absent inside. Russian translation performs worse than other languages according to reviews. Scan limits apply. Translation history does not clear.
apps.loved: Fast text translation for language pairs available without a subscription.
apps.weak: The advertised core feature (photo and camera translation) requires payment to access. The language set does not match what is shown in marketing.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended. The gap between what is promised and what is delivered is too wide.

apps.title: Translate Anything
apps.verdict: An app advertising voice and camera translation where neither works reliably. Live translation freezes mid-phrase, camera translation does not translate at all. Automatic charges with no price disclosure, and canceling the subscription from within the app is impossible.
apps.loved: The conversational interface for a live phone translation is conceptually well designed.
apps.weak: Voice recognition cuts off mid-word, and there is no way to switch the language pair without restarting the app.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended in its current state.

quotes.text: I am enjoying the app but it often misunderstands my attempt at voicing the sentence or word I am trying to have translated making me have to type in the word or sentence even if I repeat it several times slowly and with good annunciation.

I have been using Google to send messages to Russian speakers and they tell me that the English to Russian translation produces too much nonsense that is unreadable to them. While I can view Russian to English and mostly get a sense of what they are trying to tell me, there are still too many flaws.

scenarios.name: Tourists and travelers
scenarios.job: Read a menu, a sign or instructions in a foreign language and talk quickly with a local on a trip
scenarios.gap: Reviewers discuss offline access and history. It helps to test downloading languages and opening a saved translation without a connection.

scenarios.name: Immigrants and foreigners in a country not their own
scenarios.job: Explain themselves to a doctor, an official, a neighbor or an employer every day, without having learned the country’s language
scenarios.gap: In the reviews, noise and the disappearance of access to a mode are what get in the way. What helps is a saved pair, a way to repeat a phrase and the option to read the recognized original.

scenarios.name: People learning a language
scenarios.job: Understand an unfamiliar word or phrase right in the context of reading, a film or a conversation and remember it without switching apps
scenarios.gap: Reviewers want to save words, alternatives and pronunciation. The starting combination is to translate a phrase, mark a word and come back to it in context.

scenarios.name: Professionals and business users
scenarios.job: Translate a business letter, a contract or a technical manual precisely, keeping the tone and the terminology, often right inside a work messenger
scenarios.gap: In the reviews, context and settings that survive are what matter. What helps is a personal dictionary, a comparison of options and an original that stays available for checking.
